An agent here is a role with one job. Each agent has its own model, its own prompt, and a list of tools it's allowed to use. In Java terms, think of it as a small service. The prompt is its contract. The tools are its only side effects. The Loom script is what wires several of these together.

Your project has one agent, **Helper**. It runs on `gemini-2.5-flash` and has no tools, so it can only read text and answer in text. It can't send, write or call anything. That makes it a safe first agent. I've opened the graph on it.

The script checks clean, the audit shows no findings, and the golden dataset and scripted tests exist. Tests and mock runs cost nothing. No paid run has happened yet.

The next step is the harness. It's a short `HARNESS.md` that decides the run's bounds, when it counts as done, and what happens if it fails. Your budget is currently 50,000 tokens and 10 calls. The harness is where you decide whether those numbers are right.

Do you want me to explain the harness in more detail, or draft the instruction for the builder to write `HARNESS.md`?
